primitives.name: Customer Value Tier
primitives.verbatim_quote: # Implementation Notes — Pricing Sprint (Increment 1) ## Shipped this increment (config + tests + docs — all green, additive, inert) - `apps/web/lib/pricing/value-architecture.ts` — 4-tier customer value ladder (Free/Pro/Elite/Operator), POSITIONING + EMOTIONAL_VALUE, prices sourced from `pricing-phases.ts` FOUNDING (no drift).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T': 'tier index ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3} for {Free, Pro, Elite, Operator}', 'P(T)': 'probability of customer transitioning to tier T'}
primitives.assumptions: Each tier corresponds to a unique set of features and pricing phase; no drift in foundational tiers.

layer2.mapping: The tier hierarchy mirrors a partially ordered set where each tier is a superset of lower tiers, enabling monotonic feature inclusion.
layer2.telemetry: Feature unlock rate per tier observed during user onboarding.

primitives.name: Feature Access Control
primitives.verbatim_quote: - `apps/web/lib/pricing/feature-gates.ts` — feature-gating map: 26 features with customer explanation, minTier, status (live/demo/preview/waitlist/planned), freePreview + lockBehavior, upgrade CTA.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F': 'set of 26 features', 'f ∈ F': 'individual feature', 'minTier(f)': 'minimum required tier for feature f', 'lockBehavior(f)': 'access restriction type for feature f'}
primitives.assumptions: Features are strictly gated by minimum tier; free preview allows limited access without subscription.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Features are unlocked only when minTier(f) ≤ current tier.

layer2.mapping: Feature gate logic is derived from the value ladder, mapping each feature to its corresponding tier threshold.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of users accessing features above their tier level.

primitives.name: Promotional Code Enforcement
primitives.verbatim_quote: - `apps/web/lib/pricing/promo-codes.ts` — 7 promo codes, all INACTIVE + UNAPPROVED, non-stackable, with compliance + kill-switch metadata.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C': 'set of promo codes', 'c ∈ C': 'individual promo code', 'active(c)': 'boolean indicating activation status', 'stackable(c)': 'boolean indicating stacking capability'}
primitives.assumptions: All promo codes are inactive by default; no Stripe integration for coupon creation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Promo codes are enforced via backend validation before application.

layer2.mapping: Promo code system enforces a binary constraint similar to feature locks—either active or inactive—with metadata for compliance.
layer2.telemetry: Number of attempted promo code applications versus approved usage.

reasoning_traces.think:
The value ladder operates as a discrete topological space where each tier T_i represents an open set under inclusion, forming a nested sequence of increasing feature access. The operator 'minTier(f)' maps features to this lattice, ensuring that higher tiers always include all lower-tier features. Feature gate logic acts as a projection function from the full feature space onto the subset accessible at any given tier. Promotional codes introduce a conditional override mechanism, modeled as a Boolean filter applied pre-subscription. These primitives form a coherent system where tier membership determines feature availability, and promotional overrides are constrained by compliance rules. Failure modes include leakage of paid features to Free users (prevented by tests), incorrect tier assignment (guarded by price-drift checks), and unauthorized promo use (enforced via kill-switches).
